title: District Attorney prosecutions for public corruption and fraud on public funds, 2011 to 2026
question: How often has the District Attorney filed public-corruption and public-fund fraud charges, how did those cases end, and how long did they take?
finding: Of 102,791 new criminal cases the District Attorney filed on 2011-2026 arrests, 59 carry a public-corruption charge (misappropriation by an officer, false claim to a public body, bribery of an officer, or a Government Code conflict of interest): 42 from 2011-2019 arrests and 17 from 2020-2026, 12 of them from 2024-2026. Of the 38 resolved, 24 ended in conviction (63%), against 51% of all resolved cases and 63% of felony theft and forgery cases; the median case took 640 days from filing to resolution, against 183 for all cases. 9 are still pending. Fraud on public or insurance funds: 225 cases, 83 of 116 resolved convicted (72%).
how: Cases prosecuted (dcjk-vw8q): new criminal filings only, one per court number, by arrest year; the motions to revoke probation are left out because they carry the charges of the original case. Case resolutions (ynfy-z5kt): one row per court number, outcome from case_status, days from filing_date to disposition_date. A case counts in a row when any filed charge has the number shown; one case can count in several rows. The files give the charge number without the code it belongs to; the code in each label is read from the number (1090 and 87100 are not Penal Code crimes; 1871.4 exists only in the Insurance Code). Baselines: every resolved case, and felony cases whose most serious crime type is theft or forgery.
limits: A charge is not a conviction, and a case listed here proves nothing about anyone. The files hold cases built from arrests and referrals; cases the State Attorney General or federal prosecutors bring are not in them, and Medi-Cal provider fraud is mostly the State's. Charge lists are incomplete for some cases: 269 filings carry a charge coded "NA", and at least one public-corruption filing on this site (court number 26007118) lists only three perjury counts although the District Attorney announced conflict-of-interest counts. 7,305 filings have no status. Records sealed under Penal Code 851.92 and similar rules show as "Record Sealed" or as a dismissal. "Dropped for a plea in another case" (Penal Code 1385) means the person pleaded guilty in a related case, so the conviction share understates how many ended in some conviction. Counts are small; a few cases move the percentages.
